title: Jeremy Corners
author: Isaac Banner
notes: The Caller's Box 20362, permission: full. The author's own note: "Author recommends you not call this dance." And the one that decides how it is encoded: "Square through is done in a diamond formation." A two-pass record, the second pass the same with the twos active; the set progresses at the end of each pass, which is what makes the second pass's own selections the next neighbour along. **The square through's foursome is written out** (M9b, DD31): `"who": "self+partner+N1+N2"`, the written relation list `docs/dance-record.md` now documents, is the transcript's "[with twos, W1, and N2 M1]" - four dancers named one at a time and out of two minor sets, which no tag, station list or single relation could say. Both passes write it, so the second pass's `[with N2]` is the same four one progression along. **Measured before and after, and it changes none of the gated oracles**: closure passes at 2, 4 and 6 couples and fails at **37.7359 px** at 3 and 5 either way, reach passes at every length either way, and collision fails at **0.000 px** at every length either way. The one number it does move is `progressed`, 32.0000 -> 37.7359 px at 2 couples. **Both of M9b's owed things are closed** (M9c), and neither was the square through. (a) The `wait-out -> diamond` seam at beat 192 was **32.0000 px, exactly the width of the set**: the waiting couple's crossing really does swap it across, and `planCycle`'s model never learned - the fill that plans a `wait-out` runs after every call, so a pass boundary handed the next pass a couple it still had on the other line. The outs now write back at a pass boundary as well as at a call that carries the progression, and **closure passes at 0.0000 px at every checked length**, where 3 and 5 couples failed at 37.7359. At two and four couples nobody ever waits, which is the whole of why only the odd lengths showed it. (b) B2's single-file promenade is written for three of the four (`who: ["1L","2L","2R"]`) and was planned on a ring of **four**: `{ number: "dancers" }` answered 4, a third of the ring snapped to a quarter turn, and `2L` finished on the place `1R` had been standing on since beat 32. A figure is now planned over the dancers it has (`resolve.ts`'s `castGroup`), the ring is a ring of three with a 120 degree step, and **the beat-56 collision is gone at every length**. **Still owed, one thing, measured: collision 0.000 px at beat 48**, `c0/lark ~ c1/robin` - B1's balance and swing is a gatherer and settles the ones on to the nearest two home places, (16, 20) and (-16, 20), while the twos are still standing on them: `c1/robin` has not moved from (16, 20) since beat 32 and `c1/lark` is stranded at (-6.011, 26.288), because A1's diamond and A2's contra corners leave the inactive couple off its station. At six couples the worst is instead at beat 128, `c4/lark ~ c5/robin`. **Two readings still unsettled by measurement.** (1) The second token of "Square through 2 (NR;SRNL)" could not be read. The first is a neighbour by the right; the second is written here as the partner by the left, because a square through's second hand is with somebody other than the first and a partner is who that is in a diamond. (2) "Ones turn contra corners (along the set)" is `axis: "along"`, which swaps which corner is first. `axis: "across"` was measured too and closes at 32.0000 px at 2, 4 and 6 couples against 37.7359 at 3 and 5, so the transcript's own word is kept and the other reading is a pixel or two better at half the line lengths. Neither changes the motion: `turn-contra-corners` runs a hand at **297.4 px/beat** against a bound of 68.4 either way, because after the diamond the actives are standing in the middle of the set and their corners are a whole dancing place and a half away. **FR-B1 rebuilt A1 and A2.** (1) *The diamond is a shape, not a figure* (DD41): the user, "its not a move. its a place setup. it means that the whole minor set is rotated 1/8 turn basically." So the `diamond` figure id is gone and A1's first eight beats are four ordinary calls - pass through across, turn alone a quarter to the right, cast back round one, and a second turn alone carrying `"form": { "shape": "diamond", "at": "point" }`, which is the transcript's own "step into center and face partner in distance; form diamonds". The shape settles the ones on the two places of the hands-four that a turn of an eighth puts along the set, and leaves the twos on the two it puts across it. (2) *Contra corners is danced by six* (DD45): `"who": "ones"`/`"twos"` and no `axis`, because the corners are now the two diagonals in the couples above and below rather than two dancers of the same minor set, which is what the user's "can only be shown correctly with 6 dancers" means. **Measured after, at 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 couples**: closure passes at 0.0000 px everywhere (as before); `progressed` is 37.7359 px everywhere (as before); reach passes at 2, 3, 5 and 6 and **fails at 1.9009 px at four couples**, beat 142.375, `c1/lark`'s left - the second pass's interrupted square through in the new diamond, which is the figure M9e already had at 0.7543 px of collision on the same beat; collision fails at every length as it did before, and its worst has moved from B1's balance and swing at beat 48 to **A1's cast back at beat 6** (`c1/robin ~ c2/lark`, 0.000 px at 2, 4, 5 and 6 couples; 5.422 px at three). One more thing worth writing down: the `pass-through` that opens A1 is a geometric pairing, and at four couples and up the **second** pass's twos are standing side by side on one line rather than across the set from each other - the neighbour swing that ends the first pass put them there - so nobody is opposite them and they stand for those two beats (`kinds/pairing.ts` now leaves a dancer with nobody opposite out, as M8b's line mates already were). **Not promoted**: collision still fails at every length. **M9g: the beat-6 collision is the `cast-back`'s landing, read off a stale slot.** Measured at four couples: `cast-back`'s end is `{ point: "slot", line: "same", along: -1 }` - one dancing place behind you on your own line - and it is read off the **slot**, which A1's `pass-through` has not moved. So `c2/lark`, whose body crossed to `(-16, 40)` in the pass through, casts to `(16, 20)`: the line it left, one couple place up the set, which is `p0`'s twos' place, and `c1/robin` has been standing on it since beat 0. `collision 0.0000 px` at beat 6 at 2, 4, 5 and 6 couples. Reading the landing off the body instead lands it on `(-16, 20)`, which is where `c1/lark` stands, so the slot is not the whole of it either: **one dancing place behind is the next minor set, and in this dance the couple there is standing still.** The diamond the four beats are walking toward is `p2`'s own, centred on `(0, 50)`, and `c2/lark`'s place in it is `(-4.24, 31.62)` - 23 px back from where the cast leaves it. It is A1's shape (FR-B1's, and `figure-review.md` has the diamond awaiting the user's eye), so the proportions are not touched here. `progressed` is 37.7359 px at every length - across the set and a place along - so the dance could not be promoted on the collision alone.
